thought_title: Seeing a Church Through Its Ministers

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Ἐπεὶ οὖν ἠξιώθην ἰδεῖν ὑμᾶς διὰ Δαμᾶ τοῦ ἀξιοθέου ὑμῶν ἐπισκόπου καὶ πρεσβυτέρων ἀξϊων Βάσσου καὶ Ἀπολλωνίου καὶ τοῦ συνδούλου μου διακόνου Ζωτίωνος, οὗ ἐγὼ ὀναίμην, ὅτι ὑποτάσσεται τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ὡς χάριτι θεοῦ καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ ὡς νόμῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: Since, then, I was counted worthy to see you through Damas, your bishop who is worthy of God, and through your worthy presbyters Bassus and Apollonius, and through my fellow slave the deacon Zotion, may I have joy of him, because he submits to the bishop as to the grace of God, and to the presbytery as to the law of Jesus Christ.
pass_b_english: So I have been granted the privilege of seeing you, through Damas, your bishop, a man worthy of God; through your worthy presbyters, Bassus and Apollonius; and through my fellow slave Zotion, the deacon. May I have joy in him! For he is subject to the bishop as to God's grace, and to the presbytery as to the law of Jesus Christ.

choices.why: Ignatius uses slave language of himself as a condemned man and of church ministers; 'servant' softens it.

choices.english: May I have joy in him!
choices.why: Optative wish of benefit and delight; a short exclamation keeps his warmth.
rejected: whose friendship may I ever enjoy

choices.english: granted the privilege of seeing you, through ...
choices.why: He sees the whole church in its delegates; 'through' keeps διά.
The Greek sentence never reaches a main clause; English turns the 'since' clause into a statement instead of supplying a verb.

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF supplies '[I now write to you]' to finish the broken sentence; we restate instead of adding. ANF spells the deacon 'Sotio'; Lake's Greek has Ζωτίων (Zotion).

notes: The Greek sentence is an anacoluthon (no main verb); Pass B restates without adding a claim.
Source spelling ἀξϊων (diaeresis) reproduced as supplied.

review.notes: Checked paragraph [1] only: Ἐπεὶ οὖν ἠξιώθην ἰδεῖν ὑμᾶς διὰ Δαμᾶ τοῦ ἀξιοθέου ὑμῶν ἐπισκόπου καὶ πρεσβυτέρων ἀξϊων Βάσσου καὶ Ἀπολλωνίου καὶ τοῦ συνδούλου μου διακόνου Ζωτίωνος, οὗ ἐγὼ ὀναίμην, ὅτι ὑποτάσσεται τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ὡς χάριτι θεοῦ καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ ὡς νόμῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Pass A keeps the sense: 'Since, then, I was counted worthy to see you through Damas, your bishop who is worthy of God... may I have joy of him, because he submits to the bishop as to the grace of God, and to the presbytery as to the law of Jesus Christ.' Pass B neither adds a claim nor reverses it: 'So I have been granted the privilege of seeing you, through Damas... May I have joy in him! For he is subject to the bishop as to God's grace, and to the presbytery as to the law of Jesus Christ.' Agents (Ignatius seen as worthy; Zotion submits), optative wish, and bishop-as-grace / presbytery-as-law distinctions hold. No negation in the Greek; no quoted scripture or citation to mismatch. Title names the thought, not only the locus. Anacoluthon of Ἐπεὶ οὖν is disclosed; B does not invent a main verb.

Source paragraph 1: Greek matches Ignatius Magnesians 2 (Lake 1912 Loeb). Pass A renders all clauses: worthiness to see via Damas (ἀξιόθεος ἐπίσκοπος), worthy presbyters (Βάσσου καὶ Ἀπολλωνίου), fellow slave deacon (συνδούλου μου διακόνου Ζωτίωνος), optative wish (ὀναίμην), submission to bishop as grace of God (ὑποτάσσεται ... χάριτι θεοῦ), and to presbytery as law of Christ (νόμῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ). Pass B preserves sense: 'granted the privilege of seeing you, through Damas, your bishop, a man worthy of God; through your worthy presbyters, Bassus and Apollonius; and through my fellow slave Zotion, the deacon. May I have joy in him! For he is subject to the bishop as to God's grace, and to the presbytery as to the law of Jesus Christ.' No omission, addition, or contradiction. Negation, agency, modality, doctrine preserved. No scripture citations to verify. Title 'Seeing a Church Through Its Ministers' names the thought. Notes disclose anacoluthon and spelling.
